answer.summary: Sri Batchu’s recommendations imply building the growth system in this order: establish shared goals and fast-learning habits, focus teams on metrics they can influence, then run quick experiments and scale the ones that work. This is a synthesis, not a fixed roadmap he lays out.

sections.heading: Set the foundation
sections.content: Prioritize culture, rituals, and cadence over finding a perfect team structure. Agree on one or, at most, two simple north-star metrics, and build a culture of data-driven hypotheses, quick execution, MVPs, and learning from failure.

sections.heading: Make goals actionable
sections.content: Choose a growth-level metric that is motivating, intuitive, and close enough to the work for the team to affect. Then give local teams metrics they can directly influence, with a finance-and-data translation layer connecting those metrics to the overall north star. At Instacart, growth rallied around monthly active orders, while individual teams had more directly actionable measures.

sections.heading: Run experiments, learn, and scale
sections.content: Work cross-functionally and at a fast cadence: Ramp’s growth team used two-week sprints and cross-prioritized rather than working in silos. Test ideas—including cross-channel bets—on a smaller scale; invest more when they work. Batchu also describes growth as a diversified portfolio of bets, managed for reasonable ROI and guided by experimentation and data.
